title: Pad Thai
subtitle: Stir-fried rice noodles with prawns, egg, and tamarind
excerpt: Thailand's most famous noodle dish: rice noodles stir-fried with prawns, egg, bean sprouts, and a sweet-sour-savoury sauce of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar, finished with peanuts and lime.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pad Thai was promoted by the Thai government in the 1930s and 1940s as a national dish designed to reduce rice consumption and promote national identity through a unified street food. It is now the dish most associated with Thai cooking internationally. The sauce is built from three key ingredients: tamarind paste for sourness, fish sauce for saltiness and depth, and palm sugar (or brown sugar) for sweetness. The balance of these three elements is what makes pad Thai taste right. Using ketchup or lime juice in place of tamarind produces an inferior result.

recipeTools.notes: A carbon steel or cast iron wok over the highest heat you have. A frying pan works but will not achieve the same colour on the noodles.

content.text: Soak the noodles rather than boiling them: they should be pliable but not fully cooked when they go into the wok. They will finish cooking in the sauce. Have everything prepared and within reach before you start cooking: the dish takes under 5 minutes once the wok is hot and there is no time to stop. If you do not have tamarind paste, mix 2 tablespoons of lime juice with 1 tablespoon of brown sugar as a rough substitute.

items.preparation: flat, soaked in cold water for 30 minutes, drained

content.text: Mix the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar together in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. Taste: it should be simultaneously sweet, sour, and salty.
Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the oil. Add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds. Add the prawns and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until pink.

Push everything to the sides. Crack the eggs into the centre of the wok and scramble quickly, mixing them into the prawns before fully set. Add the drained noodles and sauce. Toss vigorously over high heat for 2 minutes until the noodles are coated and have absorbed the sauce.
Add the bean sprouts and spring onion. Toss for 30 seconds more. Serve immediately, scattered with crushed peanuts, chilli flakes, and fresh coriander. Squeeze lime over at the table.
